newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu seeks extra 1.2 bln shekel budget cut.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu seeks extra 1.2 bln shekel budget cut.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Israeli cabinet was considering an additional budget cut of 1.2 billion shekels.
Treasury sources had put the additional cuts at some 1.8 billion shekels, on top of the 4.9 billion shekels of cutbacks included in the original 1997 budget of 190.8 billion shekels.

"I think the finance minister has done exceptional work and he has found several sources (of income), which do not involve raising taxes, worth over half a billion shekels," a statement released by Netanyahu's office quoted him telling the cabinet.
"But that still leaves us with a significant cut and he (Finance Minister Dan Meridor) will present this 1.2 billion shekel cut," Netanyahu said.
The cabinet was due to vote on the budget cut later on Monday.
Israel Radio said the proposal allocated expenditure reductions in percentage terms for each ministry and ministers would have until Friday to specify exactly where they would be making cuts.
The Treasury has yet to spell out publicly the proposed cutbacks.
"If we don't cut, let there be no doubt that we will pay with a deterioration in our standing in the financial markets and in our credit rating," Netanyahu was quoted as telling the cabinet session.
